Title: Need to empower Autonomous District Councils in North Eastern Region. 

SHRI JITENDRA CHAUDHURY (TRIPURA EAST): Madam Speaker, the 10 nos. Autonomous District Councils in the Northeast in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura created under the provisions of the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution need to be thoroughly revisited and an amendment of the Constitution is required to fulfill the political, social, cultural and economic aspirations of the tribal people and overall development of the region in general. The provision of the Sixth Schedule was conceived during the framing of the Constitution in early 1950s. But after that, seven decades have already passed. If we see the condition of the people there, no tangible development of those sections of the people has taken place in most of these ADC areas, leaving the exceptions in Tripura because of the pro-people policy of Left Front Government in the State even though people in general in Tripura and whole of North-East strongly feel that lot of things yet to be done in the field of social-economic spheres of this section of people, which is possible by ensuring required legislative, economic and political support from the both Centre and State. That's why to meet the cultural, linguistic and economic aspirations of tribal people in particular and the people as a whole of the region I further appeal to this Government, as this is the fourth time in row during my last three years tenure in this House. That the provisions of the sixth Schedule may be ammended to create three tier bodies like the PRI areas, urban bodies in the council areas and to make provision for allocation of adequate fund from NITI Aayog and diffrent ministries are made. Special attention has to be paid for development of the language and culture of the communities who are inhabiting in those council areas and a special project should be formulated particularly to create multi-dimensional employment oppurtunities for the benefit of the youth so that their aspirations are fulfilled and help strengthen the true process of national integration. 

माननीय अध्यक्ष : 

श्री मोहम्मद बदरुद्दोज़ा खान एवं 

श्री शंकर प्रसाद दत्ता को श्री जितेन्द्र चौधरी द्वारा उठाए गए विषय के साथ संबद्ध करने की अनुमति प्रदान की जाती है।

Title: Need to provide financial assistance to farmers engaged in Poly House Farming of grapes in Dindori Parliamentary Constituency of Maharashtra. 

श्री हरिश्चन्द्र चव्हाण (दिंडोरी) : अध्यक्ष महोदया, आपने मुझे किसानों के बारे में एक बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण विषय शून्य काल में उपस्थित करने की अनुमति दी, इसके लिए मैं आपका बहुत ही आभारी हूं।

आपके माध्यम से मेरा सरकार से कहना है कि मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र दिंडोरी में अच्छी क्वालिटी का अंगूर, गुलाब का फूल और अलग-अलग किस्म की सब्जियों का उत्पादन काफी मात्रा में होता है। मेरे क्षेत्र के अधिकांश किसानों के परिवारों का जीवन बसर अंगूर की खेती से हो रहा है। जलवायु में परिवर्तन से अंगूर की खेती पर बुरा असर पड़ रहा है। कुछ किसान पॉली हाउस फार्मिंग तकनीक से अंगूर और गुलाब के फूल की खेती कर रहे हैं। इस से अंगूर और गुलाब के फूल को खराब होने से बचाया जा सकता है और इनका उत्पादन बढ़ाया जा सकता है। किन्तु, कई किसान वित्तीय अभाव के कारण पॉली हाउस फार्मिंग तकनीक का उपयोग करने में असमर्थ हैं। 

इस संबंध में केंद्र सरकार द्वारा गरीब किसानों को आर्थिक मदद दिए जाने की आवश्यकता महसूस की जा रही है।

महोदया, मेरे दिंडोरी क्षेत्र के दिंडोरी तहसील में जैनुरी तथा अम्बे नाम के दो गांव हैं, वहां पर महारा­ष्ट्र के सबसे ज्यादा पॉली हाउस रोज की खेती होती है। वहां कम से कम 60 हेक्टेयर जमीन में किसानों ने गुलाब की खेती की है, मगर आज वे बिल्कुल घाटे में हैं। इसलिए, मैं आपके माध्यम से सरकार से विनती करना चाहता हूं कि जहां‑जहां पर पॉली हाउस की खेती है, चाहे अंगूर की खेत हो या गुलाब पुष्प की खेती हो या सब्जी की खेती हो, पॉली हाउस फॉर्मिग तकनीक का उपयोग करने के लिए केंद्र सरकार को उन सब किसानों को आर्थिक मदद देने की जरुरत है। धन्यवाद।

Title: Need to create a statutory body to preside over the compensation package for Member of Parliament. 

SHRI FEROZE VARUN GANDHI (SULTANPUR): Madam, a few weeks ago, in the National Capital, a farmer from Tamil Nadu tried to commit suicide. A few weeks before that, groups of farmers from that State to demonstrate their own suffering, held skulls farmers… (Interruptions) भैया, या तो पहले मैं बोल दूं या आप बोल दें।...(व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : प्लीज, क्या हो गया; आप बोलिए न। I have allowed you only to speak. You should not see here and there and react. You kindly address the Chair only.

SHRI FEROZE VARUN GANDHI : Madam, a few weeks before that, groups of farmers held skulls of farmers, who had committed suicide in that same State to show their misery. 

On the 19th of July, the State Assembly of Tamil Nadu accorded to itself a pay rise of 200 per cent. Without imputing any motives to this, it sent a broad message of insensitivity. 

Madam, in the first Cabinet Meeting of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru in 1952 after winning the elections, the Cabinet took a unanimous decision not to avail of their salaries for three months in the light of the economic sufferings of the people at that time. We had Members of the Constituent Assembly like Shri Biswanath Das from Odisha, who chose to draw only Rs. 25 a day as against Rs. 40 which they were entitled to, to show their sensitivity during that period. V.I. Muniswamy Pillai in 1949 in the Madras Assembly imposed a voluntary cut of Rs. 5 per diem in recognition of the suffering of the farmers, and the Madras Assembly unanimously passed the Motion.

Madam, in the Parliament of the United Kingdom on which this is largely based, there is a model of an Independent Authority, which is called the Senior Salaries Review Body, which is a body consisting of non-Parliament Members, non-politicians, academics, jurists, social welfare activities takes into account the recommendations of both the beneficiaries, that is, the Members of Parliament and the public. It takes into account the affordability and the validity of these claims, and then requests the Government for it.

Madam, such a mechanism does not exist in our country sadly. Arrogating unto ourselves the authority to increase our own fiscal compensation is not in line with the moral foundations of our democracy. Gandhiji wrote and I quote: 

“In my opinion, the allowances should be exactly in consonance with the proportion of the services rendered to the nation.” 

Madam, in the last decade, Parliamentarians had sought for an increase of 400 per cent for their compensation. 

HON. SPEAKER: What is your suggestion?

SHRI FEROZE VARUN GANDHI : Have we really earned this massive increment? 

I just want to make three points. One is that 50 per cent of the Bills in the last 15 years of this Parliament that have been passed, have not been referred to serious Parliamentary Committee deliberations, which in fact, means that the last passed Bills shows priority for politics and not policy because this House has created itself to dissect, analyze and deliberate, and then pass on policy-making.

HON. SPEAKER: In ‘Zero Hour’ only point is allowed to be raised. 

SHRI FEROZE VARUN GANDHI : Madam, just a minute more.

Madam, 41 per cent of the Bills have been passed without discussion in the last 15 years. There are those, who say that MPs should be paid in line with the private sector.

Madam, the private sector’s only motive is self-interest and profit. We are committed to the ideals of our forefathers. We are committed to make India a country of our dreams. I do not want to refer to the issues of MPs’ behaviour, performance or things such as taking cash for asking questions. I just want to make a point regarding low number of sittings and constant chaos that we witness. 

Lastly, I want to suggest that we should create an external body -- which could be a statutory body -- which presides over our compensation package or if we want to self-regulate, we should empathetically do so. Looking at the condition of the country, we should forego any increase in compensation for the rest of this 16th Lok Sabha. Thank you, Madam.

HON. SPEAKER: 

Kunwar Pushpendra Singh Chandel is permitted to associate with the issue raised by Shri Feroze Varun Gandhi.

Title: Regarding approval to Government Bill of Tamil Nadu seeking exemption of State Government quota seats from National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). 

DR. J. JAYAVARDHAN (CHENNAI SOUTH): Thank you hon. Speaker Madam. 

The introduction of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test by the Central Government has nullified the policy initiatives taken by our State Tamil Nadu to achieve specific socio-economic objectives such as creating a level playing field between the urban and the rural students and increasing public healthcare in the rural areas. The NEET had placed the students of the State Board syllabus at a greater disadvantage compared to the CBSE students. More than 90 per cent of the students are studying in State through State Board syllabus. 

Madam, the hon. Supreme Court had held that the conduct of an entrance examination does not fall within the purview of Entry 66 in List I (Union List) of the Seventh Schedule. Here, it has to be noted that the State Government’s competence to enact legislation derives from Entry 25 of List III (Concurrent List). 

Based on the legal advice received, the “Tamil Nadu Admission to MBBS and BDS Courses Bill, 2017” and the “Tamil Nadu Admission to Post Graduate Courses in Medical and Dentistry Bill, 2017” were introduced and unanimously passed in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on 1st of February, 2017. The hon. Governor of Tamil Nadu has reserved the Bills for the assent of the hon. President of India under Article 254(2) of the Constitution of India on 18th of February, 2017. 

As far as the Post-Graduate medical and dental courses are concerned, as feared, despite the assurance from the Government of India, the High Court has ruled that the time tested Tamil Nadu policy of reservation of Post-Graduate Degree courses cannot be given and the State would have to follow the MCI regulations on incentive marks and not the State pattern followed till last year leading to agitation by the Government doctors. 

The lack of assent of the two Bills passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly was one of the reasons that the State could not protect its existing policy of Post-Graduate admissions. 

Hence, I would like to request the Government of India that the approval may be accorded immediately to the “Tamil Nadu Admission to MBBS and BDS Courses Bill, 2017” and the “Tamil Nadu Admission to Post Graduate Courses in Medical and Dentistry Bill, 2017”. The accorded Presidential assent will enable the State to continue its existing fair and transparent system of admission to Government Medical Colleges and Dental Colleges in the State. 

HON. SPEAKER: 

Shrimati V. Sathyabama is permitted to associate with the issue raised by Dr. J. Jayavardhan.

Title: Need for water management of river Ravi. 

*SHRI GURJEET SINGH AUJLA (AMRITSAR): Hon. Chairman Sir, I thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak on an important matter pertaining to my constituency.

Sir I would like to draw the attention of the Government towards river Ravi that flows adjacent to my constituency. River Ravi flows along my constituency Amritsar for at least 25 kms. Pakistan falls on the other side of river Ravi. All kinds of smuggling, bootlegging and terrorism – related activities take place along this river. Whether it was the Gurdaspur incident or the Pathankot attack, terrorists used the river and this terrain to their advantage.

Sir, Pakistan has constructed a concrete embankment on its side called ‘Dhussi’. During the time of floods, our farmers suffer as they find themselves at the receiving end. The farmers of the area find themselves in dire straits financially. 

Sir, I urge upon the Government to bail out the hapless farmers of this area financially. Rivers, as such, are considered as economy – boosters in all countries. In foreign countries, rivers boost tourism as tourists come to have a canal-view or river-view in a particular area.

So, I demand that a concrete embankment should be constructed on our side of river Ravi adjacent to Amritsar constituency. A road should also be constructed along the river so that an eye can be kept on the activities of Pakistan. Secondly, over 1.50 lakh tourists visit Amritsar daily. If proper water-bodies are constructed and taken care of, these tourists will be able to enjoy the scenery. This is the area of Dera Baba Nanak Kartarpur Sahib, and Baba Buddha Sahib. It historical importance is known to all. So, I urge upon the Government to construct a concrete embankment on river Ravi. Tourism should be given a boost in the area. Farmers of the area should be bailed out economically.

श्री विद्युत वरन महतो (जमशेदपुर): सभापति महोदय, मैं अपने संसदीय क्षेत्र जमशेदपुर टाटानगर में रेल लाइन चालू किए जाने के विषय को आपके समक्ष रखना चाहता हूं। मेरा संसदीय क्षेत्र तीन राज्यों का बार्डर इलाका है, झारखंड, पश्चिम बंगाल और ओडिसा का बार्डर है। चांडील से पटौम्दा होकर झारग्राम तीन राज्यों पश्चिम बंगाल, ओडिसा और झारखंड को जोड़ेगा। चकुलिया-बोहरागुड़ा होकर बुरामरा उड़ीसा को जोड़ेगा, यह काफी पुरानी मांग है। टाटानगर से बदाम पहाड़ होते हुए क्योंझर जो ओडिसा को जोड़ेगा, इसे डबल लाइन करने की जरूरत है। तीनों रेल लाइन का कार्य काफी दिनों से पेन्डिंग है। मैं इस महत्वपूर्ण विषय को सदन में रख चुका हूं। आपके माध्यम से माननीय मंत्री जी से मांग करना चाहता हूं कि जनहित को देखते हुए तीनों रेल लाइनों को अविलंब चालू किया जाए, जिससे लोगों के आने-जाने और उद्योग चलाने में कठिनाई न हो।

Title: Need to give tax exemption under Section 80 C of Income Tax to parents having two girl child. 

कुँवर पुष्पेन्द्र सिंह चन्देल (हमीरपुर): सभापति महोदय, मैं एक बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण विषय सदन के संज्ञान में लाना चाहता हूं। नारी शक्ति का जितना सम्मान भारत में है उतना अन्यत्र कहीं भी नहीं है, चाहे विकसित देश हो या विकासशील देश। हमारी संस्कृति ने दुनिया को संदेश दिया है। हमारी संस्कृति से प्रभावित होकर अनेक विकसित विचारधाराओं वाले देशों की महिलाएं भी भारतीय नारी जैसा सम्मान पाने के लिए अपने देश की नागरिकता लेने के लिए उत्सुक हैं। हमारी संस्कृति का मानना है कि यत्र नार्यस्तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवता। 

महोदय, प्रजातंत्र के इस मंदिर में हम लोग जब कोई भी बात रखते हैं तो पूरे देश के संज्ञान में आती है और सरकार भी उसे संज्ञान में लेती है। प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में बेटी बचाओ बेटी पढ़ाओ का कार्यक्रम पूरे देश में चल रहा है, उससे हमारी बेटियों का मनोबल बहुत बढ़ा है। इससे लोग प्रोत्साहित हो रहे हैं, चाहे उज्ज्वला की योजना हो, आवास योजना हो या राशनकार्ड हो अनेकों योजनाओं से बेटियों को बहुत सम्मान मिल रहा है। मैं प्रधानमंत्री जी का जी टेलीविजन पर एक कार्यक्रम देख रहा था। महिलाओं की क्रिकेट टीम क्रिकेट खेल कर वापस आई, उसका एक कार्यक्रम था। उसमें एक बेटी ने बोला कि मुझे सबसे अच्छा तब लगा जब प्रधानमंत्री जी ने मुझे ट्वीट किया। 

मेरा आपके माध्यम से भारत सरकार से अनुरोध है कि हमारे प्रधानमंत्री जी बेटियों के लिए सब कुछ करना चाहते हैं तो माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी एक ऐसा प्रावधान कर दें कि जिस परिवार में केवल बेटी या दो बेटी है और बेटे नहीं हैं, ऐसे माता-पिता को आयकर की धारा 80 सी की डेढ़ लाख रुपये की सीमा को बढ़ाकर ढ़ाई लाख या तीन लाख रुपये कर दिया जाए।

Title: Issue regarding increasing incidents of stalking in the country. 

SHRIMATI KIRRON KHER (CHANDIGARH): Thank you, Sir, for giving me this opportunity. Stalking in India is still considered a problem rather than a serious crime. We focus on the supposedly bigger problems of crime, while stalkers roam around with impunity, no shame in their creed.

Delhi, Telangana, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh see numerous cases of stalking crimes. Through 2014, there were 4700 complaints of stalking in Delhi. Two such recent instances in Delhi ended up in murders. The same man had stalked them for years and then stabbed them to death because they turned down his marriage proposal. Can you not penalize this stalker before he becomes a murderer? Do we only notice when the offence becomes fatal?

Female students stalked outside colleges, working women stalked after work. We need to see stalking as a precedent to assault. It needs to be regarded as violence against women.

Trivializing incidents of invasive stalking will actually make them more serious with time. It will be wiser and cognizant of us to realize the gravity of the rise in this crime and become units of assistance to every victim who is prey to this violence. 

A senior prosecutor of the city police pointed out that stalking cases are complex and often do not end in conviction, resulting in the accused coming out and posing a bigger threat. Moreover, women are afraid and reluctant to register complaints about stalking. What good are laws if the ability to act on them is forever absent?

डॉ. रमेश पोखरियाल निशंक (हरिद्वार)ः भारत के संविधान के भाग- 17, राजभाषा अध्याय- 1, संघ की भाषा के अंतर्गत अनुच्छेद- 343 संघ की राजभाषा शीर्षक के तहत (1) संघ की राजभाषा हिन्दी और लिपि देवनागरी होगी। संघ के शासकीय प्रयोजनों के लिए प्रयोग होने वाले अंकों का रूप भारतीय अंकों का अंतर्राष्ट्रीय रूप होगा। संविधान के उक्त अनुच्छेद खंड-1 में किसी बात के होते हुए भी इस संविधान के प्रारंभ से 15 वर्ष की अवधि तक संघ के उन सभी शासकीय प्रयोजनों के लिए अंग्रेजी भाषा का प्रयोग किया जाता रहेगा जिसके लिए उसका ऐसे प्रारंभ से ठीक पहले प्रयोग किया जा रहा था। इतना ही नहीं संविधान में स्पष्ट है कि 15 वर्ष से पूर्व भी यदि राष्ट्रपति चाहेंगे तो संघ के शासकीय प्रयोजनों में भी किसी के लिए अंगेजी भाषा के अतिरिक्त हिन्दी भाषा का और भारतीय अंकों के अंतर्राष्ट्रीय रूप के अतिरिक्त देवनागरी का प्रयोग प्राधिकृत कर सकते हैं, किन्तु ऐसा भी नहीं हो सका। भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 345 के तहत हिन्दी को अधिकारिक रूप से राजभाषा के रूप में मान्यता दी गयी है साथ ही यह व्यवस्था की गयी है कि 15 वर्ष तक राजकीय कार्य हेतु हिन्दी का उपयोग किया जायेगा। दुर्भाग्य है कि आज 67 साल बीत जाने पर भी स्थिति ज्यों के त्यों बनी हुई है। हिन्दी हमारी राष्ट्रभाषा ही नहीं बल्कि देश को एकता में पिरोने का एक सूत्र है। प्राचीन और भारतीय संस्कृति की मूल प्राण देववाणी संस्कृत है और हिन्दी का उद्भव इसी संस्कृत से हुआ है। विश्व में 100 करोड़ से अधिक लोगों द्वारा बोली और समझी जाने वाली हिन्दी भाषा आज अत्यंत दयनीय स्थिति में है। आज हिन्दी के उत्थान पर गंभीर प्रयासों का अभाव है। जब जर्मनी विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी और प्रबंधन की शिक्षा जर्मन भाषा में दे सकता है, चीन चीनी भाषा में, जापान या रूस अपनी भाषा में तो भारत ऐसा क्यों नहीं कर सकता है? आज जब न्यूयार्क, शिकागो, जर्मनी, जापान, आस्ट्रेलिया, इंग्लैंड में हिन्दी भाषा पर कार्य हो रहा है, तो हम अपनी ही भाषा के प्रति इतने उदासीन क्यों हैं?

मैं सरकार पुरजोर आग्रह करता हूँ कि हिन्दी को संविधान की मूल भावना के अनुरूप राजभाषा के रूप में स्थापित कर संघ के शासकीय प्रयोजन के लिए अनिवार्य रूप में प्रयोग मे लाये जाने का कानून सुनिश्चित किया जाए।

Title: Need to provide compensation to the coconut growing farmers.

Title: Need to provide special financial package to Government of Tamil Nadu for Erode-Palani State Highway. 

SHRI S. SELVAKUMARA CHINNAIYAN (ERODE): The expansion of Highway connecting Erode and Palani via Kangeyam and Dharapuram is very important for the people of Kongu region. A survey for expansion of Erode-Palani Road via Kangeyam and Dharapuram was undertaken through Tamil Nadu Road Sector Project. 

The Erode-Dharapuram Highway (SH 83A) being one of the high-traffic density roads is being considered for the Public—Private-Partnerships (PPP) for expanding the road width from the existing seven metres to 10 metres.

The project would help substantially since the bottleneck and traffic jams created at many places would be removed. The road is divided by a median, but there is meagre scope for simultaneous passage of two vehicles on either side. 

The road is very important for hundreds and thousands of Devotees who perform padayatra during Thai Poosam and Pan guni Utthiram festivals along the 100 Kms road stretch between Erode and Palani via Kangeyam and Dharapuram. This road stretch being narrow at many places become root cause for many accidents and death of several pilgrims every year. It will be very useful for pilgrims as well as for regular pedestrians if the road is extended on both sides and a pathway is constructed with provisions for resting and relaxing, particularly toilets along this road. 

Therefore, I urge the Union Government to provide a special financial package to Government of Tamil Nadu to execute the expansion of the road on both sides from Erode to Palani via Kangeyam and Dharapuram.

Title: Regarding Avinashi Athikadavu Ground Water Recharge Project in Tamil Nadu. 

SHRI C. GOPALAKRISHNAN (NILGIRIS): Avinashi Athikadavu Ground Water Recharge project aims at channelling the surplus water from Pilloor dam during the monsoon season to all the high and dry areas of Coimbatore, Tirupur and Erode districts. The Pilloor dam water would be allowed to flow for 35km after which it would be diverted through two canals at Achampalayam. 

The State Government has announced Rs 250 crore in the Budget for the land mark project, which is estimated to cost Rs 2,500 crore. The State has already allotted Rs 3.27 crore to kick-start the project. 

Tender for environmental feasibility study for the project, has been awarded to WAPCOS, a mini ratna public sector enterprise under the aegis of Union Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation. 

While the procedure can’t be skipped for a medium irrigation project, it can be put on fast-track. We hope the Centre will do its bit to implement the project that had been pending for the past 60 years. Farmers, however, continue to be sceptical about the implementation of the project. 

Hence I urge upon the Government to do its bit to implement the project.

I also further request to conduct feasibility study for Pandiyar- Meyyar Scheme.

Title: Regarding full utilization of funds under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). 

DR. TAPAS MANDAL (RANAGHAT): One of the main reasons for the farmers' distress and crop failure is due to the lack of proper irrigation system in place. Since the inception of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) in 2015, the total funds allocated was Rs. 20,925 crore whereas the promised allocation was 30,000 crores. The revised estimates of funds so far been allotted depict the reality of improper utilization at the ground level. In the year 2016-17, government drastically reduced the budget allotted for the PMKSY by approximately Rs. 2,000 crore to Rs. 5,767 crore. Above this, the revised estimates of the scheme is Rs. 5,187 crore only i.e. 51% of the promised average allocation. 

Under this project with a tag line of “Har Khet Ko Pani (More Crop Per Drop)”, the Central Government allotted an average of Rs. 7,000 crore per year for the whole country. It must be noted that in Bengal, the budget for Irrigation and Waterways is Rs. 2,140 crores for 2017-18. Moreover, the State has also initiated a scheme called “Jaltirtha” for addressing the problem of irrigation coverage. So far a budget of approximately Rs. 500 crore has been spent by the government under 'Jaltirtha' with emphasis on surface water management in the state. 

Therefore, it is imperative that the Government completely utilize the funds allocated under PMKSY to ensure welfare of farmers across the nation.

Title: Regarding the issue of gender equality. 

SHRI GAJANAN KIRTIKAR (MUMBAI NORTH WEST): Issues concerning crimes against women need to be tackled on a priority basis so that there is social justice and security. Madam, though there are laws to protect women from all sources of violence and to sensitise the public on this issue but still crimes against women are on the rise. In this connection, I refer to the National Crime Records Bureau data which state that a total of 3,27,394 cases of crime against women were reported in the year 2015, which was an increase of over 43 per cent since 2011. 

In order to check increasing crimes against women, the Government should go to the root of the problem; and if possible come forward with stringent legislation. Besides this, there is a need to bring about change in mindset to respect women and to ensure gender justice. One thing I would suggest for the consideration of the Government is right from childhood years children should be sensitised to respect women as they are taught to respect men. In fact, gender equality should be made a part of the school curriculum. The school teachers and parents should be given training to conduct regular personality building and to keep a watch on the actual behaviour of the children to make them gender sensitive.

Title: Regarding unemployment situation in the country.

This includes skilling, reskilling and upskilling of the workforce to improve employment oppoitunities. Majority of our workers are in informal sector. I request the government to consider more innovative ways for inclusion of workers from informal sector to formal sector. SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL (ALAPPUZHA): Mr. Deputy Speaker, Sir, I would like to point out some serious concerns relating to the economic situation of this country. 

As we all know, even after nine months, the common people in the country have not come out of the shock of demonetization. Let us look at some statistics. Sir, India’s economic growth sought for the fourth consecutive quarter in three months, which ended in March, according to the data released by the Government, GDP growth slowed to 6.1 per cent in a fiscal fourth quarter from 7 per cent in the third. Real Gross Value Added (GVA), another measure of economic growth, slowed to a pace of 5.6 per cent in the March quarter. Fiscal fourth quarter growth in the 2.3 Trillion Dollars Indian economy, the third largest in Asia, trailed 6.9 per cent. Because China grew in January-March, India is losing the status as a world’s fastest growing economy. India’s per capita income in real terms in 2016-17 also slowed at the pace of 5.7 per cent to Rs. 82,296 against 6 per cent last year. 

This growth rate was unexpected as the Central Statistics Office earlier in January had estimated 7.1 per cent growth as compared to the 7.6 per cent in 2015-16. The construction sector strengthened 3.7 per cent in March quarter as compared to 3.4 per cent growth in the preceding quarter. This is a very alarming picture. This was like shooting on the tyre of fast moving cars. The ill-thought decision to demonetize 1000 and 500 rupees notes is still making negative impact upon the economy. The smoothly going economic growth of the country was badly affected. Unprecedented rate of unemployment is there. Even now, black money and fake currency is circulated. More interestingly, even the Government is unaware of the actual impact of the demonetization so far. 

Our learned Finance Minister is here. When demonetization was announced, outside Parliament and inside Parliament, hon. FM narrated the advantages of demonetization. Four issues have been highlighted by you. One, demonetization will certainly address the menace of black money. Second, it will definitely address the concern of fake currency. Third, it will increase the usage of digital currency. Fourth, it will reduce terrorism. These four points were highlighted by the hon. Finance Minister and the hon. Prime Minister when demonetization was announced. Let us have a discussion and an analysis on that. 

Sir, the ruling party said that demonetisation was a surgical strike on black money. They widely used it for political gains. They claim that it will boost the economic growth in the country, that it will end all types of extremism in the country. But the actual figures give a very opposite picture. The Government is not giving any answer to the basic questions even after nine long months have passed. We the Members of Parliament have a right to know the exact figures. The Government has a duty to inform the Parliamentarians the exact figures on three points. How much demonetised currency has come into the banking system after demonetisation? How many new notes have been printed so far? How much black money is unearthed? We expect answers to these three major questions from the Finance Minister today. 

More than two times the RBI has failed to produce the actual figures for the money that has come into the banking system after demonetisation. The RBI is saying that counting is still going on. We would like to know when this counting will be over. Already nine months have passed. When will the counting be completed? Please enlighten us. I seriously doubt that the Government has a motive to hide some important facts from the public of India. If most of the demonetised currency had come in, the Government’s false claim of having eliminated black money will not be correct. If more money had come in than was actually demonetised, it means more fake currency reached the banks. I, therefore, would urge upon the Government to disclose the actual figures in this House. If they cannot disclose this information in the current session, at least they can give a date as to when they are going to disclose it. 

Sir, the verdict is very clear. The main argument is that demonetisation was aimed against fake currency. We do not know how much fake currency was washed out of the system after demonetisation. The claim was that people who made money and did not pay taxes would be caught. However, the wealthiest players keep the bulk of the black money in offshore accounts and real estate. It is no surprise that the activity of faking currency is continuing even now. Interestingly, around Rs.110 crore of the Rs.610 crore of unaccounted money seized in raids during demonetisation was in new Rs.2000 and Rs.500 notes. What does it mean? That means, 70 per cent of the cash seized in raids during demonetisation was in new notes. Then where does your argument stand? Even the ruling party members were caught in Kerala printing fake money. You are aware of that. In Trichur, somebody was caught for printing fake money. There were also instances of havala transactions happening in Kerala. I am not going into the details because you know about them better than I do. 

As per the data shared by the Government in Parliament, only 1.57 lakh fake currency notes with a value of Rs.11.23 crore were detected in the country between November 2016 and July 2017. That means, 1.47 lakh fake currency notes have been seized. This is a much less number compared to the previous year. What was the figure in the previous years? In 2014-15, a total of 5.94 lakh counterfeit notes were detected as per the Annual Report of RBI. In 2015-16, this number went up to 6.32 lakh. But in this eight-month period between 9th November 2016, the day after demonetisation was announced, and 14 July 2017, only 1.57 lakh counterfeit notes were detected. I would like to have an answer from the hon. Finance Minister on this. Where is the counterfeit money? Did it just vanish like that on a fine morning in this year? 

Another argument is that demonetisation was meant for encouraging digital transactions. There is a lot of talk about digital currency. There is a lot of talk about digital transactions. What is happening there? According to official data, the number of digital transactions, which grew significantly in the aftermath of demonetisation last year, started showing a declining trend since March 2017. 

This was none other than Shri P.P. Chaudhary, the hon. Minister of State in the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, who said in a written reply in Lok Sabha that the number of digital transactions has come down from 119.07 crore in March 2017 to 118.01 crore in April and further to 111.45 crore in May 2017. It means the growth rate of digital transactions happened only because people had no other choice. 

The other argument was that it will curb terrorist activities in the country including Kashmir. What is happening in Kashmir? The situation in Kashmir is beyond our control. We are also hearing about incidents of attacks on Amarnath pilgrims. All of these show the complete failure of all claims made during demonetization. Your arguments have terribly failed. What about the jobs? According to the data released by Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy, 1.5 million jobs were lost in India during the first four months of 2017. However, the impact of demonetization is more clearly shown in the labour participation rate. The average labour participation rate was 46.9 per cent from January to October 2016.
